Article Title: Samsung Galaxy A56 5G, Nothing Phone 4a, Realme P4 Power and other midrange smartphone picks this festive season
Article Text:
Samsung Galaxy A56 5G

Nothing Phone 4a

Realme P4 Power

Vivo T5 5G

Oppo F33

The festive season is a popular time to upgrade to a new smartphone, with buyers looking for a mix of performance, camera features, battery life and value for money. The midrange segment offers several options across different price points, from Samsung 's Galaxy A56 5G and Nothing Phone 4a to the Realme P4 Power, Vivo T5 Lite 5G and Oppo F33 5G. While some models focus on high-refresh-rate displays and camera features, others stand out with large batteries and fast charging support. Prices and specifications vary across these phones, giving buyers different features to consider depending on their needs and budget. Here is a look at these midrange smartphones and their key specifications.Available at Rs 32,999, Samsung Galaxy A56 5G features a 6.7-inch Full HD+ Super AMOLED display with a refresh rate of up to 120Hz and Vision Booster support. It measures 162.2 x 77.5 x 7.4mm and weighs 198g. For photography, the phone has a triple rear camera setup comprising a 50MP main camera with autofocus and optical image stabilisation (OIS), a 12MP ultra-wide camera and a 5MP macro camera. On the front, it features a 12MP camera for selfies and video calls.The Galaxy A56 5G is available with 8GB RAM and 128GB or 256GB of storage, as well as a 12GB RAM and 256GB storage variant.Storage options may vary by market and carrier. The smartphone packs a 5,000mAh battery and runs Android 15 with Samsung's One UI 7 interface. It also comes with Samsung Knox security and an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance.Up for grabs at Rs 40,680 right now, Nothing Phone 4a runs the Snapdragon 7s Gen 4—a modest step up from the 7s Gen 3—with LPDDR4X RAM and no vapour chamber. Its 6.78-inch 1.5K 120Hz AMOLED display peaks at 4,500 nits. The camera setup is nearly identical to the Pro, swapping in a Samsung GN9 sensor for the main camera instead of the Sony unit, with Ultra XDR limited to 1080p 30fps. The (4a) sticks with a plastic frame at 8.55mm and is rated IP64. Instead of the Glyph Matrix, it gets a Glyph Bar with 63 mini-LEDs reaching 3,500 nits—40% brighter than the (3a).It also gets the larger 5,400mAh battery in India, 50W wired charging, and the same software package—Android 16 with Nothing OS 4.1, 3 OS updates, and 6 years of security patches.Realme P4 Power features a 6.8-inch AMOLED display with 1280x2800 pixel resolution. The handset is powered by an octa-core MediaTek Dimensity 7400 chipset paired with up to 12GB of RAM. The smartphone comes in two storage options 128GB and 256GB. The dual SIM smartphone runs Android 16 operating system topped with company’s own layer of Realme UI 7.0.Realme P4 Power packs a 10,001 mAh battery which comes with 80W fast charging support. The smartphone houses a dual rear camera setup which comes with 50MP main camera with f/1.8 aperture and an 8MP ultra-wide camera with f/2.2 aperture. Front is home to a 16MP selfie shooter.Selling at Rs 34,99, Vivo T5 Lite 44W 5G features a 6.74-inch HD+ LCD display with a resolution of 1600×720 pixels, a 20:9 aspect ratio, and a smooth 120Hz refresh rate, offering up to 1000 nits peak brightness. It runs on the MediaTek Dimensity 6300 6nm processor and ships with Android 16 and Origin OS 6, supporting dual SIM (nano + nano + microSD).For photography, the T5 Lite is equipped with a 50MP Sony IMX852-AAJH5-G / LYT505C rear sensor with f/1.8 aperture, accompanied by a 0.08MP secondary sensor with f/3.0 aperture and LED flash. On the front, it houses a 5MP camera with f/2.2 aperture. Security is handled by a side-mounted fingerprint sensor.Oppo F33 5G features a 6.57-inch Full HD+ AMOLED display with a resolution of 2,372 × 1,080 pixels and a pixel density of 397ppi. It is powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 6360 MAX processor, an octa-core chipset with a clock speed of up to 2.4GHz. The smartphone runs Android 16 and comes with 6GB of RAM and 128GB of internal storage.For photography, the Oppo F33 5G has a dual rear camera setup comprising a 50MP primary sensor and a 2MP secondary camera. On the front, it features a 16MP camera for selfies and video calls. Camera modes include Portrait, Night, Panorama, slow-motion video, time-lapse, dual-view video and Pro mode. The phone packs a 7,000mAh battery.
Article Summary: The midrange segment offers several options across different price points. Prices and specifications vary across these phones, giving buyers different features to consider depending on their needs and budget. Samsung Galaxy A56 5G is available with 8GB RAM and 128GB or 256GB of storage. Nothing Phone 4a runs the Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 with LPDDR4X RAM and no vapour chamber.

Article Title: As Michael Dell thanks Jensen Huang ‘with a bunch of history’, Nvidia CEO calls him pride of …
Article Text:
Michael Dell responds with 1985 throwback

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell recently engaged in a warm public exchange reflecting on the formative years of the personal computer industry. Both the executives traded nostalgic memories with Hunag highlighting Dell’s early beginnings and long-standing manufacturing ties with Taiwan. Praising the billionaire founder, Huang looked back on how the availability of Taiwanese PC hardware and chipsets opened the doors for entrepreneurial pioneers, singling out Dell as a defining success story and calling him the “pride of Austin.” Recalling how Dell got his start in the hardware business, Huang outlined how accessible components enabled a young college student to launch what would become a global tech powerhouse.“What started out as Compeq, IBM, because of Taiwan PC chipsets were available to all kinds of companies, including this little kid named Michael Dell. He just bought motherboards from Taiwan, assembled them into a PC, bought an operating system, licensed an operating system from Microsoft and he became a PC maker,” Huang said.Huang emphasised Dell's deep-rooted connection to the island's tech ecosystem, adding, “Michael has a relationship in Taiwan that goes way back.He's from Austin, Texas, pride of Austin, and he's a good guy. What a nice man. Great human being.”Acknowledging Huang's remarks, Michael Dell took to social media to thank the Nvidia CEO while sharing archival details of his earliest visits to Taiwan and the hardware behind his very first machines.“Thanks very much @JensenHuang! My first trip to Taiwan was in 1985 when I was 20,” Dell wrote, pointing out that Taiwanese printed circuit board manufacturer Compeq (not computer company Compaq) was instrumental in producing early components for his nascent operation.“Compeq (not Compaq 😂) made PCBs for us. This is the hand wired (Jay Bell, RIP) prototype of our first 286 based PC and the actual production motherboard,” Dell shared.Dell also pointed out how the global semiconductor landscape looked different prior to the rise of foundry giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC): “It was based on a chipset from Chips and Technologies, they were produced in Japan at that time before TSMCs rise. I explained a bunch of this history in #PlayNiceButWin.”
Article Summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell recently engaged in a warm public exchange. Both the executives traded nostalgic memories with Hunag highlighting Dell’s early beginnings and long-standing manufacturing ties with Taiwan. Huang looked back on how the availability of Taiwanese PC hardware and chipsets opened the doors for entrepreneurial pioneers.

Article Title: Chinese researchers set optical fiber world record with speed equal to downloading 20,000 4K movies in one second
Article Text:
30% performance jump in a single year

If and when the technology is deployed commercially, the 3.2 Pb/s capacity could allow 3.2 million households to run simultaneous gigabit-speed broadband connections.

connections. The throughput is approximately 3.2 million times faster than a standard one-gigabit consumer internet line.

Spatial division multiplexing and multi-band transmission

A joint research initiative in China has set a new world record for real-time data transmission across optical fiber, reaching a staggering 3.2 petabits per second (Pb/s) over a 24-core cable. The breakthrough achieves data throughput fast enough to download more than 20,000 4K movies in a single second, according to an announcement published on the official government portal for Hubei Province (via Tom’s Hardware). The milestone has been achieved through a collaboration among several leading Chinese technical bodies and optical firms, including the National Key Laboratory of Optical Communication Technology and Network (under the China Information and Communication Technologies Group), Pengcheng Laboratory, and Fiberhome Fujikura Fiber Optic Technology Co., Ltd.The newly-recorded 3.2 Pb/s benchmark surpasses the previous real-time optical transmission record of 2.5 Pb/s set by the very same research coalition earlier this year. That shift represents an almost 30% performance improvement achieved in under 12 months, highlighting rapid progress in high-capacity communication architectures.To put the volume into everyday perspective:From an engineering perspective, the 3.2 Pb/s trial validates the practical viability of combining spatial division multiplexing (SDM) with S+C+L multi-band transmission technology across a multi-core fiber structure.During development, the research team had to navigate significant technical bottlenecks. The first was preventing signals traveling down adjacent cores inside the 24-core line from bleeding into and corrupting one another.The second was managing the distinct transmission behaviors, operational tolerances, and technical specifications across the combined S-, C-, and L-frequency bands simultaneously.What separates this achievement from conventional laboratory benchmarks is its deployment design. The 3.2 Pb/s figure was delivered in real-time using commercially compliant hardware architectures. As the setup adheres to real-world commercial standards, the framework could be practical and deployable across enterprise and public networks in the near future.By contrast, purely academic laboratory trials running across similar 24-core telecommunications cables have charted speeds as high as 5.29 Pb/s. However, those higher theoretical thresholds depend heavily on specialised experimental signal processing techniques and non-standard laboratory equipment.
Article Summary: A joint research initiative in China has set a new world record for real-time data transmission across optical fiber. The breakthrough achieves data throughput fast enough to download more than 20,000 4K movies in a single second. The throughput is approximately 3.2 million times faster than a standard one-gigabit consumer internet line.

Article Title: Japanese companies compensate users after waves of hacking hit business and economic stability
Article Text:
AI hacking (Representative image)

$50 million crypto ransom demanded and rejected

Japanese companies are moving to pay financial compensation directly to affected users following a relentless wave of cyberattacks that has paralysed digital services, compromised customer databases and sparked broader concerns regarding national economic stability. According to a report by news agency Reuters, leading the corporate response, GMO Internet Group, a major digital financial and infrastructure services conglomerate, announced that customers will be fully reimbursed for financial losses resulting from unauthorized access following an attack on its foreign exchange trading platform. Additionally, the company will distribute a goodwill payout of 5,000 yen (around $32) to every customer, group CEO Masatoshi Kumagai revealed.Reflecting on the escalating danger facing online operations, Kumagai issued an assessment of the modern digital landscape.“The internet itself is now starting to break down. The internet is increasingly being transformed into a tool that malicious actors use to threaten and rob people,” wrote Kumagai, whose business footprint spans internet infrastructure, web domains, and cryptocurrency trading platforms.In an update published on Monday (October 26), Kumagai revealed that the suspected hackers behind the breach issued a financial extortion demand, threatening to publicly leak confidential corporate records and customer data unless the company paid $50 million in cryptocurrency.GMO stated that it will not give in to the extortion demand and is coordinating its incident response closely with law enforcement and regulatory authorities. The company did not draw any link between its breach and the PHP software vulnerabilities that forced public portals offline worldwide last week.Beyond financial payouts, GMO plans to offer a complimentary alternative service to clients for six months. While white-hat security researchers contracted by the firm had previously identified system weaknesses, Kumagai acknowledged that the depth and velocity of internal remediation were insufficient to head off the intrusion.Meanwhile, the mounting corporate fallout has drawn a response from Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who confirmed that the administration plans to compile an emergency package of counter-cyberattack measures by next week. As part of a defensive strategy, the government announced that it will establish a specialised unit tasked with simulating AI-driven attacks to expose structural flaws across enterprise and public networks before malicious actors can weaponize them.The initiative follows widespread domestic disruption after critical bugs disclosed in the foundational PHP language triggered millions of automated exploitation attempts globally.Kumagai urged Tokyo to take an aggressive stance under its newly established cyberdefense framework, which took effect this month. Such countermeasures could include offensive actions, such as targeting hostile external command servers to disable threats at their source.
Article Summary: GMO Internet Group, a major digital financial and infrastructure services conglomerate, announced that customers will be fully reimbursed for financial losses resulting from unauthorized access. The company will distribute a goodwill payout of 5,000 yen (around $32) to every customer, group CEO Masatoshi Kumagai revealed.

Article Title: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees in India, US, UK and Canada; HR head Amy Coleman tells staff: Eligible employees will receive an email with...
Article Text:
"This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support,"

"another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs,"

Microsoft's voluntary exit offer pays out like its standard severance

Buyouts now sit alongside layoffs in Microsoft's AI-era job cuts

Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees across India, the US, the UK and Canada, its second voluntary exit programme this year and a much wider one than the first. Announced on Monday in a memo from Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, the Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) covers more than a quarter of the company's roughly 223,000 employees. It reaches up to level 70 on Microsoft's internal scale, which takes in general managers and some staff with vice president titles, though not corporate vice presidents.Unlike the retirement buyout Microsoft ran earlier this year, this one has no age or tenure cut-off, and performance plays no part in who qualifies. Eligible employees will get an email with their individual terms within hours. They have until the first week of December to decide, and those who accept will leave at the end of the year.Coleman wrote. It also gives participating organisationsshe added.The package matches Microsoft's standard severance. That means base pay linked to tenure and level, continued stock vesting, healthcare for a fixed period and career transition support. What it leaves out is the extended healthcare that made the retirement programme an easy yes for many long-serving staff.Severance in Microsoft's US layoffs earlier this year started at 60 days of base pay and went up to 39 weeks for most employees. Staff at level 64 and below got a week of base pay for every six months of service, while levels 65 to 67 got two weeks.Not every team is in. Business leaders decide whether their groups participate, and sales is sitting this one out. Marketing, commercial business, security, and discovery and quantum teams are excluded too, according to people familiar with the matter. Copilot, CoreAI, Windows + Devices, Xbox, finance and HR are among those taking part, while Cloud + AI and Microsoft AI are partially in.The VEO builds on the Voluntary Retirement Program from this spring, the first in Microsoft's history. That offer went to roughly 8,750 US employees at senior director level and below whose age and years at the company added up to at least 70. About 30% took it, and Microsoft booked a $900 million charge for it in April.The turnout helped shrink the layoffs that followed, Coleman said later. Microsoft still cut 4,800 jobs in July, about 2% of its workforce, and several hundred more in September, after cutting over 15,000 in 2025. Headcount stood at 223,000 on June 30, down from 228,000 a year earlier.The company is under pressure to hold down operating costs while it spends tens of billions on data centres and AI infrastructure. Still, Microsoft says the buyout is not a sign it needs fewer people, nor a replacement for layoffs, which remain on the table. It expects a much smaller share of employees to accept this time.Quarterly earnings on Wednesday could offer a first look at what the offer will cost. Coleman called the programme "new for us" in her memo, and said in July that Microsoft was studying whether voluntary exits could become a regular, even annual, fixture. How many of these 60,000 employees take the deal will likely settle that.
Article Summary: Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees across India, the US, the UK and Canada. It is its second voluntary exit programme this year and a much wider one than the first. Eligible employees will get an email with their individual terms within hours.

Article Title: Days after Elon Musk said that Tesla-SpaceX merger would be a 'good idea', one of UK's largest banks send note to investors saying …
Article Text:
In pic: Elon Musk

“With a combination heavily expected, and with expectation for some premium to Tesla stock, we believe this should drive upside for the stock,”

“I think it would be a good idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies,”

Why Barclays expects a merger to benefit Tesla shares

“a key part of the Tesla bull case,”

Tesla’s other businesses supported the upgrade

Barclays has issued a new bullish call on Elon Musk’s Tesla. The British bank upgraded the electric vehicle company’s shares from Equal Weight to Overweight and raised its price target from $370 to $450. An Overweight rating indicates that an analyst expects a stock to outperform other companies in the same sector. The new target suggests about 21% upside from Tesla’s closing price last week. Analyst Dan Levy said growing expectations of a merger between Tesla and SpaceX drove the upgrade, though he also pointed to potential improvements in Tesla’s car, energy, and Robotaxi operations.Levy wrote in a recent note to investors, which was reviewed by CNBC. His assessment came days after Musk discussed the potential transaction on a SpaceX earnings call.Musk said. Tesla shares rose about 2% in premarket trading after Barclays upgraded the stock.Both companies have created committees of independent directors to consider a possible combination. Musk leads Tesla and SpaceX and holds large stakes in both, so he's a conflicted party and can't participate directly in the committees’ discussions.Barclays expects any transaction to include a premium for Tesla shareholders, meaning SpaceX could offer them shares valued above Tesla’s market price before the deal. Levy described the potential merger asreferring to the reasons investors may expect the stock to rise.However, no agreement has been announced. Musk warned investors not to assume a merger is certain, and shareholders of both companies would need to approve any deal. The Associated Press reported that Musk played down the possibility of an imminent transaction.Barclays considers an all-stock acquisition of Tesla by SpaceX the most likely structure. Under that arrangement, Tesla investors would receive SpaceX shares instead of cash.Levy said Tesla’s automotive business could return to growth this year after two years of declines. He expects further gains in 2027 from Full Self-Driving adoption and increased exports from the company’s Shanghai factory.Tesla has also said its energy business is almost fully booked for 2027 because of demand from data centres. Barclays believes demand could boost energy-storage shipments by more than 50%.The bank also cited a recent increase in miles travelled by Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet. Levy said the change gave him more confidence that the service could compete with Alphabet-owned Waymo.Barclays’ $450 price target and Overweight rating remain the bank’s assessment, not a confirmed outcome. Tesla shares were still down more than 17% year-to-date before the upgrade.
Article Summary: Barclays has issued a new bullish call on Elon Musk's Tesla. The British bank upgraded the electric vehicle company’s shares from Equal Weight to Overweight and raised its price target from $370 to $450. Analyst Dan Levy said growing expectations of a merger between Tesla and SpaceX drove the upgrade. Levy described the potential merger asreferring to the reasons investors may expect the stock to rise.

Article Title: Apple launches new iPad mini with bigger OLED screen and A20 Pro chip: Price in India, features and more
Article Text:
The new iPad mini starts at Rs 82,900 in India

A20 Pro makes the iPad mini much faster at AI and gaming

iPad mini price in India now starts at Rs 82,900

Two years after a quiet chip bump, the iPad mini is back with a proper redesign. The new iPad mini moves to an 8.5-inch OLED display, up from 8.3 inches, and pairs it with the A20 Pro chip, IP67 water and dust resistance, and a 5.4mm body that is thinner and lighter than before. Pre-orders open in India on October 28, with sales starting November 6.The timing stands out. Apple announced the tablet two days before its "Pro and tell" event on Wednesday, giving the smallest iPad a spotlight of its own. It is also the first proper redesign since 2021, after the 2024 model arrived as mostly a chip and storage refresh.The footprint stays the same despite the bigger screen, thanks to bezels that are 24% thinner. Peak brightness climbs to 1,200 nits, more than double the previous model, and the display can dim to just 1 nit for late-night reading. A nano-texture glass option, until now limited to the iPad Pro, is also available to cut glare outdoors.Built on a 2nm process, the A20 Pro has a 6-core CPU and a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in every core. Apple claims up to 4.5x faster AI performance, 2.7x faster graphics and 60% quicker multithreaded performance over the last generation.The 512GB variant adds a Dual 16-core Neural Engine for heavier on-device AI tasks like running local language models.The iPad mini also supports Siri AI, arriving in beta with iPadOS 27.2. The 12MP Center Stage front camera moves to the landscape edge, fixing the off-centre framing on video calls. Apple's N1 chip adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and cellular models get the C2 modem with up to 50% faster data speeds. A new Acoustic Display routes bass through the screen for fuller sound.The Wi-Fi model costs Rs 82,900, while the Wi-Fi + Cellular version is priced at Rs 1,00,900. Students can get it from Rs 76,900 with education pricing. The 2024 iPad mini went on sale at Rs 49,900, before a price hike earlier this year took it to Rs 69,900.The tablet comes in midnight and starlight, with 128GB, 256GB and 512GB storage options. The new TechWoven Smart Folio costs Rs 8,500, and both the Apple Pencil Pro (Rs 11,900) and Apple Pencil USB-C (Rs 7,900) are supported.
Article Summary: The new iPad mini moves to an 8.5-inch OLED display, up from 8.3 inches. It pairs it with the A20 Pro chip, IP67 water and dust resistance, and a 5.4mm body that is thinner and lighter than before. Apple announced the tablet two days before its "Pro and tell" event.

Article Title: Days after laying off nearly 1,000 employees and firing two top executives, Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters tells staff: Two things can be...
Article Text:
Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters addresses staff after layoffs

Netflix fires content chief Bela Bajaria and film head Dan Lin

Why Netflix is cutting jobs despite rising profit

Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters has a message for employees after a rough October: the company is doing well, and it also needs to do better. Speaking at a staff town hall this week, Peters said “two things can be true,” according to a Bloomberg report.He described Netflix as a growing, profitable business that rivals would envy, but admitted there is more work to do to push growth further. The remarks come less than two weeks after the streaming giant cut nearly 1,000 jobs and fired two of its most senior content executives. Bloomberg calls it Netflix’s biggest round of job cuts and executive turmoil in five years.The layoffs were announced on October 14 in a memo from Peters and co-CEO Ted Sarandos. They cover about 6% of the workforce, with product, technology, legal and human resources teams hit hardest. Netflix had around 16,000 full-time employees at the end of 2025.The same afternoon, Sarandos called chief content officer Bela Bajaria into his office around 4:30 pm. He told her she was out, and that former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice would take over her role.Bajaria, who spent a decade at the company, skipped the Season 3 premiere of Nobody Wants This that evening and never went back to a Netflix office, Bloomberg reports.Film chief Dan Lin was dismissed two days later.Talent appears to be the sticking point. Sarandos told analysts that Rice understands talent relations. According to Bloomberg, long-time partners like the Duffer Brothers and Shawn Levy have moved to other studios, while David Fincher chose not to renew his deal.On paper, the business looks healthy. Netflix is still growing at double digits and is on pace for about $15 billion in profit this year, per Bloomberg.Viewing is the problem. Subscribers are watching on fewer days each month and spending less time on the service overall. In its shareholder letter, Netflix said members watched over 97 billion hours in the first half of 2026, only 2% more than a year earlier. The company also won its fewest Emmys in a decade.Wall Street is split. Morgan Stanley praised the company for acting decisively, while Pivotal Research said its concerns remain unchanged. Netflix shares fell 6.6% last week, largely because of a weak forecast for the end of the year.Peters’ town hall message may settle nerves inside the office. Investors, though, will be waiting for the growth he says Netflix still has to find to show up in the next set of numbers.
Article Summary: Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters says the company is doing well and needs to do better. The remarks come less than two weeks after the streaming giant cut nearly 1,000 jobs and fired two of its most senior content executives. The layoffs cover about 6% of the workforce, with product, technology, legal and human resources teams hit hardest. The company won its fewest Emmys in a decade.

Article Title: The State that Elon Musk tells every company in America to move to has suspended 17 data center construction permits over …
Article Text:
Data center (Representative image)

Automated portal kept ‘rubber-stamping’ mega-projects

Abbott audits 1,800 facilities to protect grid and water resources

Texas, the business-friendly destination that tech billionaire Elon Musk routinely urges American companies to relocate to, has suspended the construction permits for 17 data center projects and taken an automated approval portal offline after state regulators discovered permits were still being handed out weeks after an official freeze was ordered. The intervention comes after Texas governor Greg Abbott called for a complete halt on new data center approvals in September 2026. Despite that directive, automated systems continued approving applications, prompting public reports from watchdog groups FracTracker Alliance and Public Citizen that revealed more than two dozen approvals had slipped through the cracks, according to a report by 404 Media.In response, state regulators pulled the plug on the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality’s (TCEQ) automated licensing software, known as STEERS (State of Texas Environmental Electronic Reporting System). A notice posted on the state website confirmed the shutdown:“TCEQ’s electronic filing application used for automatic authorizations has been temporarily shut down to ensure all applications are reviewed by agency staff to determine if they are related to data centers.”The STEERS platform had long functioned as a digital mechanism to quickly grant routine construction clearances. However, when Abbott instructed agencies to pause new data center authorisations, state officials failed to take the automated software offline. As a result, applications continued moving forward without manual administrative oversight.All 17 of the suspended authorisations involve stormwater construction permits, which is a mandatory regulatory step in Texas where builders level and grade the earth.Securing this clearance is an essential requirement for nearly any major commercial construction development to proceed legally in the state.The permit freeze follows Governor Abbott’s decision to put the brakes on roughly 1,800 data center projects across Texas while state agencies conduct exhaustive operational audits. The widespread pause was prompted by mounting alarms over the massive energy and water demands of high-density computing hubs, as well as their broader environmental consequences for neighboring towns.“Our top priority is to protect Texans’ safety and quality of life. Any project that fails to comply with the requirements set forth by the PUCT and ERCOT, and by state law, must be denied connection to the Texas grid. Simply put, Texans must come first,” Governor Abbott said in an earlier statement explaining the audit.Under the governor’s directives, any proposed facility failing to meet the standards set by the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT), the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), and state statutes will be formally blocked from linking up to the Texas electrical grid.Earlier this year, a report claimed that Texas is all set to become the world’s new data center capital. Research from Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL) claimed that the state is on track to surpass Virginia as the world’s largest data market by 2030. Tech giants Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Meta are expected to spend more than $600 billion in 2026 in AI infrastructure expansion.
Article Summary: Automated portal kept ‘rubber-stamping’ mega-projects. Governor Abbott audits 1,800 facilities to protect grid and water resources. Tech giants Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Meta are expected to spend more than $600 billion in 2026 in AI infrastructure expansion.

Article Title: Dell expands AI factory with NVIDIA, announces new agentic AI solutions and infrastructure
Article Text: Dell Technologies has unveiled a broad set of updates to its Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, introducing new agentic AI solutions, deskside AI offerings, validated ecosystem integrations and purpose-built infrastructure aimed at helping enterprises move AI projects from experimentation to production. The company said more than 6,500 customers have now adopted the platform, up from 5,000 in the previous quarter.The announcement comes as enterprises increasingly look to deploy agentic AI systems that can reason, make decisions and perform tasks autonomously. Dell said the latest expansion of its AI portfolio is designed to provide organisations with greater control over their AI infrastructure, data, models and operations while addressing concerns around costs, governance and return on investment.According to the company, the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA combines infrastructure, software, ecosystem partnerships and managed services to help businesses deploy AI workloads on infrastructure they own and control. The company argued that enterprises are prioritising end-to-end AI lifecycle support and are seeking alternatives to cloud-only deployments.As part of the update, Dell announced that Reflection's Beam open-weight model has been validated on the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, giving enterprises access to an Apache 2.0-licensed model designed for software engineering and long-horizon agentic AI workloads.Dell also expanded its AI ecosystem through integrations with partners including Dynatrace for AI observability, Mistral for knowledge assistants and agentic AI platforms, and Fogsphere for computer vision applications. The company said the ecosystem now spans AI models, applications and operating systems, including support for SUSE Linux.The company additionally highlighted a multilayered security architecture that combines hardware-rooted infrastructure, NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture and Red Hat AI Factory software to help enterprises securely deploy autonomous AI agents at scale.Dell also expanded its Dell Deskside Agentic AI portfolio with new validated deployment templates designed to help businesses scale AI workloads from a single developer workstation to deployments of more than 1,000 systems. The new solutions include blueprints for agentic coding, AI-powered workflows, NVIDIA NemoClaw deployments, Hermes Agent implementations and higher-education AI lab environments.On the hardware front, Dell announced a new 64GB unified-memory configuration of the Dell Pro Precision with GB10, aimed at developers and smaller teams working on local AI development projects. The company said systems can be clustered together to support larger AI models and more complex workflows. Dell also disclosed that the Dell Pro Precision with GB300 workstation will soon be available with Windows support, delivering up to 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaflops of FP4 compute performance.To support growing AI workloads, Dell introduced several new infrastructure offerings.Among them is the Dell Modular Data Center with NVIDIA DSX POD, a containerised, factory-integrated AI infrastructure design that includes compute, storage, networking, power and liquid cooling systems aimed at accelerating AI deployments.The company also announced the Dell PowerEdge M9882, a server platform featuring 256 NVIDIA Vera CPUs in a single rack designed for agent orchestration, code execution and other AI execution workloads. For mainstream enterprise environments, Dell introduced the Dell PowerEdge R8822, an air-cooled server optimised for agentic AI workloads, data processing, analytics and reinforcement learning.Another addition is the Dell PowerEdge XE9810, which Dell said will provide rack-scale inference capabilities using Groq 3 Language Processing Units for high-throughput production AI deployments. The company also unveiled new NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) platforms running on Dell PowerEdge servers, targeting telecom operators that want to run radio access network and AI workloads on a shared infrastructure.
Article Summary: More than 6,500 customers have now adopted the platform, up from 5,000 in the previous quarter. Dell said the latest expansion of its AI portfolio is designed to provide organisations with greater control over their AI infrastructure, data, models and operations.

Article Title: Slack co-founder Stewart Butterfield met Marc Benioff for barely an hour before the $28 billion sale; Benioff never used Slack, reveals early employee; Butterfield’s last meeting with him was cut shor
Article Text:
Slack co-founder Stewart Butterfield and Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff met for barely an hour before the $27.7 billion Slack sale.

Salesforce offered Slack more than double its share price

Marc Benioff praised Slack Huddles but did not use the app himself

A Davos panel with will.i.am pushed co-founder Butterfield out of Salesforce

Slack co-founder Stewart Butterfield spent barely an hour with Marc Benioff before Salesforce agreed to buy Slack for $27.7 billion in 2020. The last of those meetings ended early because a Hollywood star walked in. The detail comes from Johnny Rodgers, a former Principal Engineer at Slack and one of its earliest employees, who has been documenting the company’s story on his Building Slack blog.“I only got about one hour of total facetime with Marc before the deal was announced. My last meeting with him was cut short because McConaughey arrived,” Butterfield told Rodgers for the second part of his Salesforce series. That is Matthew McConaughey , whom Salesforce reportedly pays $10 million a year to be its spokesperson. Rodgers also writes that it was clear inside the company that Benioff himself did not use Slack and did not quite get it.The deal came as a surprise to most of Slack. In the first part of the series, Rodgers recalls an untitled calendar invite from Butterfield in late 2020, sent to the company’s original team. On the Zoom call, Butterfield asked how they would feel about selling Slack to Salesforce at $45 a share. The stock was trading around $22 at the time.The approach had come from Bret Taylor, then Salesforce’s chief operating officer, in the late summer of 2020. Slack was nearing $1 billion in annual recurring revenue, and the pandemic had made it a default tool for remote teams. At $27.7 billion, it was the second-biggest software acquisition ever at the time, behind IBM’s $34 billion purchase of Red Hat.Benioff publicly called it “a match made in heaven”.The deal closed in July 2021. Butterfield reported to Taylor, who soon became co-CEO alongside Benioff. The plan was for Taylor to run day-to-day operations while Benioff stayed on as the founding face of the company.Huddles, the quick audio calls Slack rolled out in mid-2021, became its first big feature under Salesforce. Benioff singled it out at a company all-hands and praised how fast the team had built it. But Benioff was not a Slack user, and that left Slack’s leaders unsure where they stood inside Salesforce.Salesforce’s sales teams had the same problem. “They didn’t understand the product. So they sold the products they understood,” Slack co-founder and former CTO Cal Henderson told Rodgers.Butterfield, meanwhile, grew frustrated with how Salesforce was run. Rodgers writes that he watched executives sign off on expensive celebrity appearances while cutting employee travel between offices. Millions were spent flying senior staff to Hawaii every year for an event called Laulima. His suggestions to Taylor and Benioff went nowhere.The breaking point came at Davos. Butterfield went expecting to meet customers on behalf of Slack and Salesforce. Instead, he was booked on an innovation panel with will.i.am, another Salesforce celebrity spokesperson. “It was so f***ed up,” he told Rodgers.Butterfield planned to announce his exit on December 1, 2022, with Salesforce executive Lidiane Jones taking over as Slack CEO. A day earlier, Taylor announced that he was leaving Salesforce. “I had no idea,” Butterfield posted internally. Rodgers believes Taylor most likely made a bid for the sole CEO job and quit when Benioff said no.Rodgers stayed on until spring 2023, ending 11 years at Slack. He is now building a new chat app called Supergroup and says one final Building Slack post is still to come.
Article Summary: Slack co-founder Stewart Butterfield spent barely an hour with Marc Benioff before Salesforce agreed to buy Slack for $27.7 billion in 2020. The last of those meetings ended early because a Hollywood star walked in. Matthew McConaughey reportedly pays $10 million a year to be its spokesperson.

Article Title: Apple Pro and tell event: Touchscreen MacBook Pro, M6 iMac, OLED iPad mini and more expected
Article Text:
Apple is expected to unveil its first touchscreen MacBook Pro at the Pro and tell event on October 28.

The touchscreen MacBook Pro brings OLED and the Dynamic Island to the Mac

M6 iMac and OLED iPad mini are expected after a two-year wait

Apple's Pro and tell event takes place in Los Angeles this Wednesday, October 28, at 10am Pacific time, or 10:30pm IST. The company hasn't confirmed what it will show, but Bloomberg's Mark Gurman expects a busy day of Mac and iPad news. Headlining the list is Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro. It will be joined by an M6 version of the entry-level MacBook Pro, an M6 iMac and an iPad mini with an OLED display.Marketing chief Greg Joswiak teased the announcements on October 19 with a short "Can't wait to pro and tell next week" post. This is Apple's second event this month. It comes two weeks after the Welcome Home showcase in New York, where the company introduced the HomeView smart display, the HomePod mini 2 and a new Apple TV 4K.Writing in his Power On newsletter, Gurman says the higher-end MacBook Pro will come in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes with an OLED touchscreen, a first on both counts for the Mac. The laptop looks similar to current models but weighs less, adds the iPhone's Dynamic Island and runs on M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. It is also expected to cost significantly more than today's top MacBook Pros.Touch will be an extra option, with the keyboard and trackpad staying central.Apple is tweaking macOS Golden Gate so that it presents controls based on whether someone has been tapping the screen or using the trackpad. Tapping a button can bring up a menu around the finger, and the Dock and Menu Bar have been reworked for touch. Gurman has said on his podcast that the laptop could go on sale on November 6.It is quite a reversal for a company whose co-founder Steve Jobs called touchscreen laptops "ergonomically terrible" back in 2010.The regular 14-inch MacBook Pro will keep its current design but move from the M5 to the M6 chip, which arrived with the Mac mini in August. Reports suggest it could pick up a hole-punch camera, along with a price increase as component shortages ripple across Apple's lineup. Gurman says a redesigned version of this model is planned for next year.The iMac is set to jump straight from the M4 to the M6, nearly two years after its last refresh. Little else is expected to change, though new colour options are possible.The iPad mini, meanwhile, could become the first iPad outside the Pro line to switch to OLED. It is expected to move to the A20 chip from the iPhone 18, and the new screen may push its price up.Apple's Mac lineup will be crowded after Wednesday, stretching from the MacBook Neo and MacBook Air to three kinds of MacBook Pro. Gurman says OLED versions of the MacBook Air and iMac are already in testing, though neither is imminent. A refreshed non-OLED MacBook Air is due early next year.
Article Summary: M6 iMac and OLED iPad mini are expected after a two-year wait. Apple's Pro and tell event takes place in Los Angeles this Wednesday, October 28, at 10am Pacific time, or 10:30pm IST. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman expects a busy day of Mac and iPad news.

Article Title: What are Neocloud providers that Elon Musk has predicted are going to see ‘guppy-level death’
Article Text:
Image credit: Cisco

“SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we’re investment grade and have Starlink & launch revenue.

That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation.

Some will make it through, but not many.”

“As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn’t have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers,”

What are Neoclouds

Benefits of neoclouds

Are there any limitations too

Narrower service portfolios: Hyperscale providers offer extensive managed services, including serverless functions, managed databases, analytics platforms, and global content delivery. Neoclouds typically focus on infrastructure-level AI services rather than full application ecosystems. This makes them less versatile for wider, all-encompassing applications.

Geographic footprint: Many neocloud providers operate in fewer regions compared to global hyperscalers. Organisations with strict data residency requirements must carefully evaluate availability.

Operational maturity: Teams accustomed to platform-as-a-service models may need additional expertise to manage lower-level infrastructure constructs such as network topology awareness or distributed training optimisation.

Integration complexity: Hybrid architectures that combine neocloud AI clusters with traditional IT systems require secure connectivity, policy alignment, and careful workload placement decisions.

Why specific neocloud weaknesses could turn into failures

Narrow service range: Neoclouds mostly sell AI infrastructure, not full application ecosystems. That leaves them dependent on AI-workload revenue, which is the profile Musk says lenders are avoiding.

Fewer regions: Many operate in fewer locations than hyperscalers. Customers with strict data residency rules may have to look elsewhere, which shrinks the pool of buyers.

Operational maturity: Teams used to managed platforms may need extra expertise to run lower-level infrastructure. That can slow adoption among firms that want simplicity.

Integration complexity: Linking neocloud clusters with existing IT systems needs secure connectivity, policy alignment and careful workload placement. Smaller firms with thinner resources may struggle to support this.
Article Summary: Neoclouds typically focus on infrastructure-level AI services rather than full application ecosystems. This makes them less versatile for wider, all- encompassing applications. Many neocloud providers operate in fewer regions compared to global hyperscalers.

Article Title: Billionaire Mark Cuban says that he is not a doomer on AI, but believes in Cockroach Theory that says spray your system with …
Article Text:
Expanding cost plus drugs into portable manufacturing

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think about the Cockroach Theory of cybersecurity? It's a valid analogy It's an interesting perspective I don't agree with it 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban said that he is “not a doomer” regarding the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), arguing that organisations can effectively protect themselves from AI-powered cyberattacks by deploying the very same technology on defense. Speaking at the Reuters Total Health conference, the former Shark Tank investor compared malicious AI agents to household pests, introducing what he called his "Cockroach Theory" of cybersecurity.“I’m not a doomer at all. We hear about the worst possible scenarios with AI, but we don’t talk about the defensive measures that that same capable AI can take against them,” Cuban said.The investor added: “It’s like the cockroach thing, right? You build a new house, you get the guys to come out and spray... the one thing I don’t want is cockroaches in my house ever. But the cockroaches find a way to get in because there’s zillions of them, right? And then if there’s one gets in, there’s more that are going to get in, and that’s kind of the way AI works.”Cuban explained that if bad actors build swarms of autonomous agents to probe networks through sheer numbers, defenders can respond with equal computational power.“It’s like the Cockroach theory, where if somebody can create enough agents, it’ll find a way to get in, and then it just exploits that.But the good news is, you can spray your systems with just as much AI,” he said, adding, “It's all brute force acts, and if it's brute force on that side with the bad guys, you can also use brute force with the good guys... And I think there’s going to be more effort from the good guys trying to stop the bad guys. ”Beyond his perspective on emerging technology, Cuban discussed the rapid evolution of his healthcare enterprise, Cost Plus Drug Company. Launched in 2022 to disrupt traditional pharmaceutical pricing, Cost Plus operates on a transparent model: charging the wholesale cost it pays for a medication plus a fixed 15% markup. In May, the business joined TrumpRx.gov, a platform established by the Trump administration to distribute discounted weight-loss medications.The venture has since broadened its footprint from retail distribution to direct manufacturing. In 2025, Cost Plus began producing sterile injectable medications commonly required by hospitals at its own dedicated compounding facility.Cuban revealed that the company has now engineered compact, tractor-trailer-sized manufacturing units that he terms “pods.” Designed to function independently or link together, these mobile units can manufacture generic medications as well as specialized treatments for rare diseases.
Article Summary: Mark Cuban compared malicious AI agents to household pests, introducing what he called his "Cockroach Theory" of cybersecurity. He said that if bad actors build swarms of autonomous agents to probe networks through sheer numbers, defenders can respond with equal computational power. Cuban discussed the rapid evolution of his healthcare enterprise, Cost Plus Drug Company.

Article Title: Stuffcool launches Giga Pro Max power bank with 100W fast charging
Article Text: Indian accessories brand Stuffcool has expanded its power bank lineup with the launch of the Giga Pro Max, a 20,000mAh portable charger designed for users who need to charge laptops, smartphones and other devices simultaneously. The new power bank combines a high-capacity battery, support for up to 100W fast charging and a built-in retractable USB-C cable, eliminating the need to carry an additional charging cable. According to the company, the device is aimed at professionals, students, travellers and users who regularly carry multiple gadgets.One of the key highlights of the Giga Pro Max is its integrated retractable USB-C cable that can be pulled out when needed and tucked away inside the power bank after use. The company says the cable includes an E-marker chip and supports up to 100W output, making it suitable for charging compatible laptops, MacBooks and other USB-C devices. The built-in design is intended to reduce cable clutter and ensure users always have a charging cable available.The Giga Pro Max supports a maximum total output of 100W and can charge multiple devices at the same time. The integrated USB-C cable can deliver up to 65W, while the additional USB-C port can provide up to 35W.This allows users to charge a laptop through the built-in cable while simultaneously charging a smartphone or another device through the USB-C port.The power bank also supports multiple charging configurations, including 65W through the built-in cable alongside 18W output from the USB-A port. Users can also connect three devices simultaneously through the built-in USB-C cable, USB-C port and USB-A port.Unlike conventional power banks focused mainly on smartphones, Stuffcool says the Giga Pro Max is designed to handle higher-power devices such as laptops and tablets. The device supports PPS charging and Samsung Super Fast Charging 2.0, making it compatible with a wide range of USB-C gadgets. The power bank houses a 20,000mAh battery rated at 77Wh and weighs approximately 407g. It measures 14.3 x 7.2 x 4.0 cm, making it relatively compact for a laptop-capable portable charger.The Giga Pro Max also features a built-in digital display that shows the remaining battery percentage, allowing users to monitor charge levels more accurately. Another notable feature is pass-through charging support, which enables users to charge connected devices while the power bank itself is being recharged.
Article Summary: The Giga Pro Max has a retractable USB-C cable that can be pulled out when needed and tucked away inside the power bank after use. The power bank houses a 20,000mAh battery rated at 77Wh and weighs approximately 407g. The device supports PPS charging and Samsung Super Fast Charging 2.0.

Article Title: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby wants the tax that made billionaires flee California across America; says: We should have a national ...
Article Text:
Scott Kirby, CEO of United Airlines

California billionaire tax debate provides backdrop

United Airlines CEO says issue is about fairness

Scott Kirby proposes mandatory national service

Thinking about future generations

Scott Kirby, CEO of United Airlines has doubled down on his controversial support for wealth tax arguing that any such policy would need to be implemented nationally rather than at the state level to prevent wealthy individuals from relocating to avoid it. According to a report by Fortune, the airline chief started the debate last week after advocating for a national wealth tax during a Q&A with The New York Times. Addressing concerns about declining public trust in corporate leaders, Kirby said growing wealth inequality poses a risk to society and requires action. "We should have a national wealth tax. It won't work by state because people will just move," Kirby said. He also suggested that inheritance taxes should become significantly steeper at higher wealth levels, adding that he would personally be willing to pay them.Kirby's remarks come as California voters prepare to decide on a proposed billionaire tax next month. Supporters of the measure argue it could become a model for other states and potentially influence broader tax policy discussions. The comments quickly drew criticism from conservative commentators and politicians, with some suggesting that Kirby should voluntarily give away a portion of his compensation if he believes the wealthy should pay more taxes.Speaking to Bloomberg Television later in the week, Kirby did not retreat from his position but emphasized that he is not attempting to shape public policy or seek elected office. Instead, he framed his argument around fairness within the tax system. According to Kirby, some individuals who derive much of their income from investments and assets can legally avoid income taxes, creating an imbalance between wealth holders and traditional wage earners.He said a more equitable system would find ways to tax the growth of wealth while potentially reducing taxes on earned income. Despite the backlash, Kirby noted that feedback he received via email was evenly divided between supporters and critics.The United Airlines chief also offered another unconventional proposal during the Bloomberg interview, advocating for some form of national service for all Americans."I think national service for everyone would be a good idea," Kirby said, suggesting that people could spend a few years serving as teachers, firefighters or members of the military.While noting that he did not serve in the military, Kirby said shared service experiences could strengthen the country and create a greater sense of civic responsibility.Kirby said his opinions on taxation, government finances and national service are rooted in concerns about the country's long-term future. "I love this country. I want it to be great for the next 250 years. I want it to be great for my kids," he said, adding that policymakers should stop pushing major challenges, including budget deficits and Social Security concerns, onto future generations.The CEO, who said he has seven children, argued that addressing those issues now is essential to ensuring future Americans inherit a stronger and more sustainable country.
Article Summary: Scott Kirby, CEO of United Airlines has doubled down on his controversial support for wealth tax. Kirby said any such policy would need to be implemented nationally rather than at the state level to prevent wealthy individuals from relocating to avoid it. Kirby also suggested that people could spend a few years serving as teachers, firefighters or members of the military.

Article Title: Anthropic's Claude accessed Georgia's public vote counts behind a paywall without human authorisation; the AI company says no individual voter records were retrieved or altered and it has added safegu
Article Text:
Anthropic's Claude accessed Georgia's public vote counts behind a paywall without human authorisation

Anthropic notified the Georgia secretary of state's office

Anthropic’s Claude bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available US ‌state of Georgia aggregate voter counts without human authorization, reported Axios. Claude accessed aggregate vote counts during a training run, pulling data that the state makes available to the public for a fee. The report quotes an Anthropic spokesperson who said that the AI model didn't access the state's voter registration system or change or pull any voting records. However, the model bypassed a paywall in accessing the information, according to Georgia officials and Anthropic."The model was being used internally for a statistics project to pull public data," the Anthropic spokesperson said as cited by the publication. "Without being asked to, the model requested a token to query a dashboard that contained information normally available for a fee. We have since put in place mitigations to block these kinds of actions."The disclosure adds to growing concerns about AI security ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.As stated in the report, the AI company led by Dario Amodei informed the Georgia secretary of state's office and the White House weeks ago about the incident.A source familiar with the matter told the publication that the administration officials urged the Georgia Secretary of State's office to make a public disclosure sooner.However, those requests went unheeded.The incident comes a month after Anthropic said in a blog post that it found examples of ​Claude "working around a restriction to reach data that ‌was ⁠gated by a token or a fee" and some of these cases involved websites run by US ​government agencies ​at the ⁠federal, state, and local levels."Claude sometimes worked around a restriction to reach data to which it did not have access. Generally, this occurred when a server refused Claude’s request, or when the data was offered only for a fee," the company then said.
Article Summary: Anthropic’s Claude accessed publicly available US ‌state of Georgia aggregate voter counts without human authorization. Claude accessed aggregate vote counts during a training run, pulling data that the state makes available to the public for a fee. Anthropic notified the Georgia secretary of state's office and the White House weeks ago.

Article Title: Dragos founder Rob Lee helped bring free cybersecurity to more than 100 utilities; now his company is joining Accenture and SANS on a $10 million plan to protect up to 500 more US water, power and gas
Article Text:
New foundation aims to protect critical infrastructure

Building on Dragos’ free programme

Rob Lee warns of growing threats

What utilities will receive

What the executives said

Accenture, the industrial cybersecurity firm Dragos and the SANS Institute have launched the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation. It is a non-profit organisation which will offer small and under-resourced US water, electric and natural gas utilities free help securing their operational technology. In its first phase, the foundation will offer cybersecurity software, hardware, deployment services and SANS training at no cost to up to 500 utilities. The three founders are making an initial combined commitment of about $10 million in funding and services, and the data company Elastic is also supporting the effort.The three organisations announced the creation of the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation, a nonprofit initiative designed to provide operational technology (OT) cybersecurity tools, deployment services, hardware support and training at no cost to eligible utilities. The programme targets smaller and under-resourced providers that often lack the funding and workforce needed to defend against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.According to the announcement, the first phase of the initiative will support up to 500 utilities serving communities across the United States. The partners said the combined investment of roughly $10 million will help strengthen services relied upon by more than 100 million Americans.The foundation builds on the Dragos Community Defense Program, which already gives more than 100 utilities free access to the Dragos Platform. Dragos was founded by Robert M. Lee, who is its chairman and CEO. Elastic’s role is technical: its Elasticsearch technology provides the main log storage and search engine inside the Dragos Platform, which helps Dragos deliver the software at scale. The foundation was announced at a roundtable on utility cybersecurity in Ohio hosted by Ohio Power Company, an American Electric Power subsidiary, together with Accenture and Dragos.Announcing the programme, Robert M. Lee said threat actors are increasingly targeting the operational environments that provide essential services to millions of Americans."Adversaries are aggressively targeting utilities, attacking the operational environments that provide life-sustaining services to millions of Americans. Yet many small operators lack the capacity to defend against these threats," Lee said. "The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation gives the utilities that need it most access to cybersecurity resources and training at no cost."Eligible US-based water, wastewater, electric and natural gas utilities with less than $100 million in annual revenue will be able to apply for the programme. Participants will receive access to the Dragos Platform, deployment and integration support from Accenture, specialised ICS and OT cybersecurity training from SANS, funding for required hardware and infrastructure, and access to a community network of peer utilities.The initiative is also being supported by Elastic, whose technology will help deliver the Dragos Platform at scale to participating organisations.Julie Sweet, Accenture’s chair and CEO, said the work has revealed a widening gap between large operators with the means to invest in cybersecurity and smaller utilities that often lack it. Lee said adversaries are aggressively targeting the operational environments that provide life-sustaining services and that many small operators cannot defend against them alone. James Lyne, SANS’ CEO, said even the best security technology will not protect a utility if its staff cannot use it, which is why the foundation focuses on training. Elastic CEO Ashutosh Kulkarni said his company is committed to helping make advanced capabilities accessible to utilities that could not otherwise afford them.
Article Summary: The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation will offer cybersecurity software, hardware, deployment services and SANS training at no cost to up to 500 utilities. The three founders are making an initial combined commitment of about $10 million in funding and services. The data company Elastic is also supporting the effort.

Article Title: In 2017, Peter Thiel famously declared Apple era is over, nine years later, he says: In my telling, after Steve Jobs ...
Article Text:
Peter Theil: Apple did nothing after Steve Jobs

Nine years after declaring Apple’s era over

Apple faces growing questions on AI

Focus turns to upcoming results

Billionaire investor and PayPal co-founder Peter Thiel has renewed his long-standing criticism of Apple, arguing that the company has failed to produce meaningful innovation since the death of co-founder Steve Jobs in 2011. According to a report by Benzinga, Theil made the remarks during a recent interview with author Walter Isaacson on The Builder’s podcast, which was released earlier this week. Theil emphasised that the smartphone was a big invention with little left to do once it was launched. After that, he said, Apple’s work was a matter of scaling the product, building the brand and extending the business over about 15 years.During the interview, Theil said that one of the biggest breakthrough of Apple was iPhone and suggested that the company mainly focused on refining and expanding the product ever since. “In my telling, it did nothing new after Jobs,” Thiel said, adding that the iPhone was such a significant invention that there was little left to revolutionise afterward. According to Thiel, Apple spent the years following the iPhone’s launch scaling the product, strengthening its brand and expanding its ecosystem rather than creating another transformative technology. Theil further added that Apple lost its sense of direction after the death of Steve Jobs.He also said that such as Elon Musk and Steve Jobs are far better for society than former Apple CEO Tim Cook.Steve Jobs introduced the original iPhone in 2007, the product was widely credited with resharing the smartphone industry and consumer technology. After almost two decades, Apple recently launched its first foldable smartphone — the iPhone Duo, making one of the company’s significant hardware shifts in years.The latest comments made by Theil echo the views he expressed nearly a decade ago. In the year 2017, Theil famously declared that Apple’s era was over, arguing that the company had reached a point where breakthrough innovation was becoming increasingly difficult.Despite the predictions made by Theil, Apple continued to grow into one of the world's most valuable companies, with its shares posting substantial gains over the years, even amid periods of market volatility.While speaking with Isaacson, Thiel argued that Apple lost its sense of direction after Jobs’ passing. He also suggested that leaders such as Elon Musk and Steve Jobs have had a greater positive impact on society than current Apple CEO Tim Cook.Thiel's criticism comes at a time when Apple is facing heightened scrutiny over its artificial intelligence strategy. The company has been working to strengthen Siri and expand its AI capabilities amid increasing competition from rivals including OpenAI and Anthropic.Apple has faced criticism over the pace of its AI rollout and challenges in delivering advanced generative AI features, an area where competitors have moved aggressively in recent years.Investors are now awaiting Apple's upcoming quarterly earnings report, which is expected to provide further insight into the company's hardware performance, AI investments and growth strategy.While Thiel remains sceptical about Apple's post-Jobs innovation record, the company's financial performance and stock market gains since his 2017 comments underscore the ongoing debate over whether transformative innovation or consistent execution is the more important measure of a technology giant's success.
Article Summary: Peter Theil made the remarks during a recent interview with author Walter Isaacson. Thiel argued that Apple lost its sense of direction after the death of Steve Jobs. He also suggested that leaders such as Elon Musk and Steve Jobs have had a greater positive impact on society than current Apple CEO Tim Cook.

Article Title: Instagram comes to Apple TV with Reels, longer videos and live shows
Article Text:
Instagram comes to Apple TV with Reels, longer videos and live shows

Instagram expands to more television platforms

How to get Instagram on Apple TV

Meta-owned Instagram is now available on Apple TV, allowing users to watch Reels, longer videos and live shows on their television for the first time. The app lets viewers watch videos from their favourite creators, discover new content and resume watching across devices. Instagram says the TV app is designed to make watching videos a shared experience for friends and family. The app requires tvOS 26.0 or later to run on Apple TV. The launch expands Instagram's video experience beyond smartphones and tablets, giving users another way to watch content on a larger screen.The Instagram app for Apple TV allows users to browse videos from creators and discover content based on their interests. Its initial TV experience focused on Reels organised into channels, with videos playing automatically.The app's description also lists longer videos and live shows, reflecting Instagram's plans to offer more than short-form content on television. Users can also resume watching videos across devices.Instagram first began testing its TV app on Amazon Fire TV devices in the US in December 2025. It later expanded the app to Google TV in February 2026 and Samsung smart TVs in June 2026. In June, Meta outlined plans to bring longer creator videos, episodic series and live broadcasts to the platform.The Apple TV launch adds another option for users who want to watch this content on their televisions.The release follows Instagram's dedicated iPad app, which launched in September 2025 after years of requests for an interface designed specifically for Apple's tablets.Users can download Instagram from the Apple TV App Store.
