Article Title: Meta is giving all its shareholders a new Class C stock, it comes after CEO Mark Zuckerberg told directors he may lose ...
Article Text:
Why Meta is creating a new share class

The California wealth tax

Months of tense negotiations

Final deal gives Mark Zuckerberg new flexibility

Trading to begin in January 2027

Meta Platforms has announced a new Class C share structure that will allow CEO Mark Zuckerberg to maintain voting control of the social media giant while giving the company greater flexibility to raise capital, fund acquisitions and compensate employees as it ramps up spending on artificial intelligence. According to a report by Fortune, the move, disclosed alongside Meta’s third-quarter earnings, comes after months of intense negotiations between Zuckerberg and a special committee of board members over how to balance shareholder interests with the founder’s desire to retain control of the company he founded in 2004. The new structure will see every existing Class A and Class B share receive one non-voting Class C share, effectively creating a two-for-one stock split.Meta has a dual-class structure in which Class A shares trade on Nasdaq with one vote each, while Zuckerberg’s holdings are mostly Class B shares with ten votes each. He holds about 60.6 percent of the voting power but only about 13.4 percent of the economic stake. If he sells Class B shares, they convert to Class A, which could erode his control.Issuing more Class A stock for employee pay, acquisitions or fundraising dilutes his voting share.Meta has long offset that with buybacks, which helped lift his voting power from 53.7 percent in 2013 to 60.6 percent now. But buybacks use cash that Meta wants for its AI build-out. Fortune says the company repurchased $26.3 billion of Class A stock in 2025, has not bought back shares for four straight quarters, and booked $21 billion in stock-based compensation in the first nine months of this year.The Class C shares carry no votes, so Meta can use them for pay, deals and capital raising without affecting Zuckerberg’s control. He can also sell some without giving up votes: 20 percent of his new Class C shares can be sold immediately, and the remaining 80 percent are “stapled,” meaning he can sell them only if he sells or converts an equal number of voting shares. Zuckerberg will still be able to elect all the directors and decide most shareholder votes.A looming California wealth tax played a central role. According to a Meta filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Zuckerberg wanted to keep voting control, meet his pledges to fund the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative with Meta stock, and be ready to pay billions to the state if voters approve the proposed tax. Proposition 40 is on the ballot on November 3. The Bloomberg Billionaires Index lists Zuckerberg at No. 5, with a net worth of $246 billion.In July, Zuckerberg told Robert Kimmitt, Meta’s lead independent director, that selling Class B shares to cover a tax bill could cut his voting stake to about 53 percent. The new Class C shares let him pay such a bill without touching his voting shares.Fortune says the plan followed months of negotiations that were sometimes contentious between Zuckerberg and a board committee that included DoorDash CEO Tony Xu, Kimmitt and former Microsoft executive Charles Songhurst. Xu disclosed his friendship with Zuckerberg but said it would not affect his judgment. The committee proposed shareholder-friendly sunset provisions that would convert Class B shares to regular stock within a year of Zuckerberg’s death or departure, or if he sold more than half his holdings. According to the filing, he refused to consider any change to his voting shares and told the committee he was “considering establishing residence outside of California.”The filing also shows that on August 4 he proposed a dividend of 20 Class C shares for every Class A and B share and that he would not accept sunsets or equity financing that diluted his control. The committee called the 20-for-1 idea excessive. By late August, with all sides dug in, committee members discussed dissolving the panel or resigning. At a September 9 board dinner, Zuckerberg told directors he planned to list his Palo Alto home for sale on September 13. The committee wanted him to stay in California, close to Meta’s AI lab.The eventual agreement reached in September represented a compromise between management and independent directors.Under the plan, shareholders will receive one Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they own. The new Class C stock will carry no voting rights but can be used by Meta for employee compensation, acquisitions and future capital raising without diluting Zuckerberg's voting influence.The arrangement also allows Zuckerberg to immediately sell 20% of his Class C shares without affecting his voting control. The remaining Class C shares are linked, or "stapled", to corresponding voting shares and can only be sold alongside equivalent Class A or Class B stock.As part of the agreement, Zuckerberg dropped a proposal seeking a founder-style compensation package and agreed to continue taking a symbolic annual salary of $1. He also committed to remaining in California or wherever Meta is headquartered for the next eight years.Meta's board formally approved the recapitalisation in October, and the company said the new Class C shares will become effective on January 19, 2027. Chief Financial Officer Susan Li said trading in the new stock class is expected to begin in late January.Speaking on Meta's earnings call, Li said the company currently has no specific financing plans tied to the new shares but wanted to ensure it had access to a broader range of funding options as it navigates an era of heavy AI-related investment."We thought it was prudent to establish the appropriate capital structure framework to ensure that we have access to a diverse pool of funding sources," Li said.
Article Summary: Meta Platforms has announced a new Class C share structure that will allow CEO Mark Zuckerberg to maintain voting control of the social media giant. The move comes after months of intense negotiations between Zuckerberg and a special committee of board members over how to balance shareholder interests with the founder’s desire to retain control. Zuckerberg will still be able to elect all the directors and decide most shareholder votes. A looming California wealth tax played a central role.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai admits that cloud business is forgoing short-term revenues to make up for ...
Article Text:
Why Google is prioritising AI research

Google Cloud customers face limited computing capacity

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the biggest challenge for Google Cloud customers? Limited computing capacity High demand for services Shortage of chips and servers 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Google is giving its AI researchers priority over cloud customers. CEO Sundar Pichai has confirmed that the company is forgoing short-term Google Cloud revenue by directing some of its limited computing capacity toward developing advanced AI models. The decision comes as demand for Google’s cloud services continues to rise and some customers struggle to secure additional capacity.“Our cloud business is at any given moment in time forgoing short-term revenues because we are making compute trade-offs to support frontier AI development,” Pichai told Alex Kantrowitz during an interview on the Big Technology PodcastFrontier AI refers to the development of models that aim to reach the highest level of current capabilities. These systems require massive computing power to train and run, creating competition between Google’s internal research and paying cloud customers.Google Cloud generated $24.8 billion in second-quarter revenue, up 82% from a year earlier, while its contracted backlog reached about $514 billion. However, Pichai said the company must maintain enough computing power for Google DeepMind’s research, and its other businesses must plan around that need.Pichai described access to computing power for Google DeepMind as “non-negotiable.” He argued that developing advanced models gives Google an early view of new AI abilities and helps the company prepare products for future uses.He also expects frontier models to help researchers build their successors through recursive self-improvement. This means an AI system assists with the research, coding, or testing required to create a more capable model.Pichai rejected suggestions that Google should focus only on smaller, less expensive models such as Gemini Flash.“We won’t do it any other way,” he said about competing at the AI frontier. “We’ve been thinking about the AI frontier for well over a decade now.”Google’s decision comes amid a shortage of the chips, servers, and data-center space needed to run AI services. Pichai said accommodating a new customer seeking computing capacity in 2027 would be “incredibly difficult to do.”“Everyone wishes you had 2x of what you had planned for,” he said, describing the shortage across the technology industry.Building additional capacity requires decisions years before customers can use it. “The compute we have today is a function of decisions I made in 2024,” Pichai said.Alphabet expects to spend $195 billion to $205 billion on capital projects in 2026, with much of that investment supporting AI and cloud infrastructure.Its regulatory filing showed that Google Cloud had $513.9 billion in contracted revenue waiting to be recognised at the end of June. Alphabet’s second-quarter filing said slightly more than half of that backlog is expected to become revenue within two years.Demand is also coming from Google’s own products. Pichai said Gemini 4 Argon processed almost 25 trillion tokens in its first 72 hours, about three times what Gemini 3 handled over the same period. He added that Google was already capacity-constrained while serving the model.
Article Summary: Google is forgoing short-term Google Cloud revenue by directing some of its limited computing capacity toward developing advanced AI models. CEO Sundar Pichai described access to computing power for Google DeepMind as ‘non- negotiable’ He argued that developing advanced models gives Google an early view of new AI abilities.

Article Title: Microsoft says 'not possible' to UK's biggest data centre developer Nscale, after repeated delays, and electricity companies promising no power supply before 2030
Article Text:
Microsoft withdraws from Nscale's Essex data centre project

“We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK, and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, in addition to other expansion sites in the UK. Our relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term, and this unfortunate London-wide grid issue has no impact on our other contracts.”

Nscale's planned IPO faces fresh challenges

Electricity shortages delay Britain's AI infrastructure plans

Microsoft has withdrawn from a major UK data centre deal. The decision is a setback for British AI infrastructure developer Nscale, which had planned to make its Loughton, Essex, facility operational next year. The project has faced repeated delays, with electricity grid operators reportedly saying power won't be available until the 2030s. Microsoft had agreed to lease 23,000 Nvidia AI chips at the site and was expected to become its anchor tenant.According to a report by The Telegraph, the withdrawal also comes as Nscale prepares for a potential US stock market listing that could value the company at up to $35 billion (£26 billion), raising questions about its expansion plans and investor confidence in AI infrastructure businesses.Microsoft recently informed Nscale that it was pulling out of the agreement announced last year. The deal was part of Microsoft's broader UK investment commitments worth £22 billion, announced during US President Donald Trump's visit to the country.The proposed facility would have housed thousands of high-performance Nvidia AI chips. However, difficulties securing electricity connections have delayed the project, forcing Nscale to look for alternative energy sources and new expansion locations.An Nscale spokesman said:Microsoft did not comment on the decision.The setback comes as Nscale considers raising billions of dollars through a potential Wall Street listing. Backed by Nvidia and other investors, the company has been privately valued at $15 billion and reportedly targets a valuation of up to $35 billion through the proposed flotation.Microsoft accounts for more than 40% of Nscale's $103 billion in contracted revenue, although the Essex project is believed to represent only a small portion of that amount. Anthropic is another major customer.Long-term commitments from major technology companies matter for data centre developers, which need substantial financing to build facilities and buy computing hardware. Losing Microsoft's commitment to the Essex site could complicate Nscale's efforts to show it can deliver planned infrastructure projects.The Loughton case study highlights challenges in developing the country's AI infrastructure, including the high cost of electricity and long delays in grid connections.Nscale has also encountered delays at a data centre project in Norway, reportedly resulting in significant penalties. Separately, OpenAI suspended plans in April for a Stargate AI facility with Nscale on Tyneside, citing Britain's high electricity prices.The wider AI infrastructure sector has faced investor concerns over rising borrowing costs and whether demand will justify the substantial spending required to build data centres. Australian rival Firmus cancelled plans for a $20 billion IPO earlier this month, citing market conditions, while other infrastructure providers have also experienced pressure on their shares and bonds.Nscale, founded by Australian entrepreneur Josh Payne two years ago, continues to pursue its UK expansion plans despite the Essex setback. The project's future will depend partly on whether the company can secure an alternative power supply and find another customer for the facility.
Article Summary: Microsoft has withdrawn from a major UK data centre deal. The decision is a setback for British AI infrastructure developer Nscale. The company had planned to make its Loughton, Essex, facility operational next year. The project has faced repeated delays, with electricity grid operators reportedly saying power won't be available until the 2030s.

Article Title: In 2018, Bloomberg founder Michael Bloomberg began funding overdose prevention in two US states; eight years later, his foundation's commitment has reached $335 million, including $150 million for six
Article Text:
In pic: Michael Bloomberg

Why prisons and emergency departments are a focus

What the initiative reports achieving since 2018

“Even one death from an overdose is too many,”

“The overdose epidemic continues to be one of the hardest public health crises our nation faces. Now is the time to accelerate this hard-fought progress, expand access to treatment, and save more lives.”

Michael Bloomberg began funding state overdose programs in 2018. Bloomberg Philanthropies initially concentrated its work in Pennsylvania and Michigan as opioid deaths contributed to a decline in US life expectancy. Eight years later, the foundation has committed a total of $335 million to the overdose crisis, including a new $150 million investment covering six states. The latest funding will continue work in Kentucky, New Jersey, New Mexico, North Carolina and Wisconsin while adding Washington, which still has one of the country’s highest overdose death rates despite recent improvements. The foundation is ending its direct work in Pennsylvania and Michigan after helping the states establish programs intended to continue independently.The foundation announced the $150 million commitment at the ninth annual Bloomberg American Health Summit in Baltimore. It will be used to make treatment for opioid use disorder available to incarcerated people and through hospital emergency departments in all six states. The program will also expand access to naloxone, a medication that can reverse an opioid overdose, and help governments direct money from opioid-related legal settlements towards treatment and prevention.People leaving prison and patients who survive an overdose face a particularly high risk of dying later. A 2007 Washington study found that formerly incarcerated people were 129 times more likely than the general population to die from an overdose during the first two weeks after release.Research published in 2018 also found that overdose survivors who received medication treatment in an emergency department were less likely to die from a later overdose. The initiative therefore focuses on providing medicines such as buprenorphine in prisons, jails and hospitals, where people at greater risk can receive treatment quickly.The six participating states are expected to make opioid-use treatment available in every prison and hospital emergency department. Washington is joining the program, while the other five states will continue to receive support.The program has helped all 24 state prisons in Pennsylvania to start offering buprenorphine. It funded an online system in Michigan that allows community organisations to order and distribute naloxone without individual prescriptions.All prisons in New Jersey and Wisconsin now provide medication for opioid use disorder. More than 75% of emergency departments across New Jersey, Michigan, and Pennsylvania have also started offering these treatments, up from an average of 28% previously.Overdose deaths in the foundation’s focus states fell almost 15 percentage points more than the national average in 2024, the foundation said. The annual report had previously noted an average 31% drop across seven participating states that year, compared to a 27% national decline.The initiative has also expanded Medicaid-covered treatment for postpartum parents in Kentucky and access to fentanyl test strips in New Mexico. It says more than half of US states now use evidence-based guidelines when deciding how to spend money received through opioid settlements.Bloomberg said.
Article Summary: Bloomberg Philanthropies initially concentrated its work in Pennsylvania and Michigan. Eight years later, the foundation has committed a total of $335 million to the overdose crisis. The latest funding will continue work in Kentucky, New Jersey, New Mexico, North Carolina and Wisconsin. Washington is joining the program, while the other five states will continue to receive support.

Article Title: Roblox founder David Baszucki and his wife turn their son's struggle with bipolar disorder into a $20 million grant for a Massachusetts hospital to study whether diet-based therapies can improve menta
Article Text:
Image via Roblox

What is Metabolic Psychiatry

Funding inspired by family's recovery

Roblox founder David Baszucki and his wife, Jan Ellison Baszucki, have turned their family's personal journey with their son’s bipolar disorder into a major philanthropic investment in mental health research. Through their family foundation, Baszucki Group, the couple has awarded a $20 million grant to McLean Hospital to establish the McLean Center for Metabolic Psychiatry. This Massachusetts-based facility will explore whether targeted nutritional and metabolic therapies, such as ketogenic diets, can improve psychiatric symptoms and brain function in patients living with severe mental illnesses.McLean Hospital, a member of the Mass General Brigham healthcare network and a primary psychiatric teaching affiliate of Harvard Medical School, announced that the centre will act as the international flagship for the newly established Global Network for the Advancement of Metabolic Psychiatry (MetPsy). The grant will also fund clinical education and physician training initiatives coordinated jointly by McLean and MH² – a clinical practice, education and training hub.Metabolic psychiatry investigates the relationship between systemic metabolism, cellular energy, brain function and mental health. While clinical neurologists have prescribed metabolic interventions, most notably the ketogenic diet, to control pediatric epilepsy for more than a century, applying these concepts to psychiatric conditions is a rapidly developing frontier.Over the past decade, an expanding volume of scientific research has indicated that metabolic therapies can positively affect both physical biomarkers and clinical psychiatric symptoms in patients diagnosed with conditions such as bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder and schizophrenia.To translate discoveries into everyday medical practice, the center will build out evidence-based clinical protocols and provider training curricula.For the Baszucki family, the funding is directly tied to their lived experience supporting their son, Matthew, through his diagnosis and treatment of bipolar disorder. Jan Ellison Baszucki, co-founder of Baszucki Group, emphasized that the personal recovery of their son through metabolic interventions inspired them to build a formal global movement around the science.“The launch of MetPsy reflects our family’s commitment to continuing to advance the field of metabolic psychiatry worldwide. As this network grows, we hope fellow funders will join us in expanding access to evidence-based metabolic interventions—a clinical approach that has restored the health and future of our son Matthew, and offers that same hope to many more,” Jan Ellison Baszucki said.To prevent clinical findings from remaining siloed, the center will anchor the MetPsy network, which connects scientists, physicians and mental health clinicians across the globe.
Article Summary: Roblox founder David Baszucki and his wife have awarded a $20 million grant to McLean Hospital to establish the McLean Center for Metabolic Psychiatry. The couple's personal journey with their son's bipolar disorder inspired them to build a formal global movement around the science. Metabolic psychiatry investigates relationship between systemic metabolism, cellular energy, brain function and mental health.

Article Title: Eric Schmidt reveals his biggest failure as Google CEO: There was a moment when Google was ahead of everybody else in...
Article Text:
Orkut and Google+ were Google’s biggest bets on social media

Eric Schmidt says being too slow was his biggest personal failing

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt has once again named social media as the one that got away. Speaking on In Good Company, the podcast hosted by Norges Bank Investment Management CEO Nicolai Tangen, the 71-year-old said Google briefly led the space during his time in charge. Losing that lead, he said, was his biggest mistake as CEO.It is a regret Schmidt has voiced before. He ran Google from 2001 to 2011, and weeks after handing the top job to co-founder Larry Page, he admitted he had seen the Facebook threat coming. “I clearly knew I had to do something and I failed to do it,” he said at a tech conference that year. “A CEO should take responsibility. I screwed up.”“There was a moment when Google was ahead of everybody else in social media. It was fairly short,” Schmidt told Tangen. “I was CEO at the time. I take responsibility for not getting ahead of that. That was a big error.”That early lead belonged to Orkut. Built by Google engineer Orkut Büyükkökten in his 20% time, the invite-only network went live in January 2004, a month before Facebook. In its first few months, more than half its traffic came from the US, with Japan a distant second.The audience shifted over the years. By 2008, Orkut was among the most visited websites in Brazil and India, two markets where it stayed popular long after users elsewhere had moved on.Facebook overtook it in India in 2010 and in Brazil in 2012, and the company closed Orkut in September 2014.Google+ was the bigger, more aggressive attempt. It arrived in June 2011, about three months after Page took over, and drew 10 million users in its first two weeks while still invite-only. That was barely 1% of Facebook’s 750 million users at the time, but the company pushed on, crossing 90 million registered users by January 2012.Sign-ups never turned into lasting engagement. After a bug exposed data from up to 500,000 profiles, the search giant closed the consumer version of Google+ in April 2019, citing low usage. Smaller efforts such as Buzz and Friend Connect had already been wound down.On the podcast, Schmidt went a step further and pointed the finger at himself rather than the company. “I think that I’m just too slow,” he said. “When I look back, everything was foreseeable. I just didn’t see it soon enough.”He said he now works in “a world of time compression”, where “the people who beat me saw it quicker than I did”.AI has only made that pressure sharper. Schmidt told Tangen that AI models take around six months to build and go out of date within five months of release. The next cycle, he said, could be measured in days.Even so, he does not claim to have fixed the habit. Talking about the AI boom earlier in the same conversation, Schmidt said he is “always not first”. He prefers to wait and see where the curve is heading before he moves.
Article Summary: Orkut and Google+ were Google’s biggest bets on social media. Eric Schmidt says being too slow was his biggest personal failing. He ran Google from 2001 to 2011, and admitted he had seen the Facebook threat coming. He said he now works in ‘a world of time compression’

Article Title: Google DeepMind builds 3D periodic table with Gemini 4 Argon: What is so different about it
Article Text:
What sets the 3D periodic table apart

Google DeepMind has revealed a way to demonstrate the capabilities of its latest artificial intelligence (AI) system: a full chemistry visualisation synched to music. Using its recently launched Gemini 4 Argon model, DeepMind generated an interactive, three-dimensional periodic table that choreographs its movements to the tempo and lyrics of Tom Lehrer’s classic 1959 song, “The Elements. ” As the fast-paced tune plays, the visualisation highlights each element in real time, displaying animated electron pathways, detailed atomic specifications, and individual light spectra.The video was shared by Google Deepmind and re-shared by Google CEO Sundar Pichai, saying, “Sound on!”. The video surfaced a week after Gemini 4 Argon’s official public debut. In an amusing nod noted by observers, a model bearing the name of the noble gas Argon was used to reconstruct the periodic table itself.Built by DeepMind’s Antigravity development platform, the project moves well past the familiar flat grid of atomic symbols found in standard chemistry textbooks. The demonstration coordinates multiple layers of data and rendering simultaneously:Each element is rendered with moving electron orbits rather than flat diagrams, and the interface presents comprehensive atomic specifications alongside the specific light emission spectra for each material.Moreover, the most technically demanding element of the demo is its timing. Lehrer’s track is famous for rattling off element names at breakneck speed. Gemini 4 Argon successfully synchronized the visual rendering, underlying scientific datasets, and audio playback to hit each vocal cue and musical beat precisely.“Gemini 4 Argon built a 3D periodic table synced to Tom Lehrer’s song, “The Elements.” Created in @Antigravity, it animates orbiting electrons, atomic data, and light spectra,” Google DeepMind said.The periodic table is not an official benchmark score, instead, it serves as a creative demonstration of how the model handles complex, multi-stage "agentic" instructions that require synthesizing scientific logic, graphic generation, and real-time audio synchronization.Gemini 4 Argon rolled out publicly on October 13, 2026, with Google DeepMind targeting the system at sophisticated operational workflows, including scientific exploration and large-scale software engineering.
Article Summary: Gemini 4 Argon model synched to Tom Lehrer’s classic 1959 song, “The Elements. ” As the fast-paced tune plays, the visualisation highlights each element in real time, displaying animated electron pathways, detailed atomic specifications, and individual light spectra.

Article Title: Explained: How YouTube watching experience is set to improve with next-gen streaming technology
Article Text:
YouTube

YouTube’s rapid open-codec shift

Unlocking multi-view and richer browser experiences

YouTube is about to enhance its video streaming experience with an upcoming move to next-generation video compression technology that promises sharper visual quality while consuming comparatively less internet bandwidth. Earlier this year, the Alliance for Open Media finalised the official specifications for the AV2 codec. Engineering projections indicate that AV2 is roughly 25% to 32% more efficient than its predecessor, AV1. In practical terms, this efficiency gain allows platforms to stream noticeably higher-definition video at existing bitrates, or maintain sharp, pristine image clarity at significantly lower bitrates, essentially cutting down total data consumption for viewers.While major streaming peers such as Netflix, Amazon, and Apple have remained silent regarding their deployment roadmaps, YouTube is moving ahead openly. According to a report by Android Authority, YouTube has confirmed plans to begin rolling out AV2 streaming as early as early 2027, targeting the web browser version of the platform first.YouTube has anchored its infrastructure around royalty-free, open-standard compression technologies.“YouTube champions open codecs that deliver the best quality video with the fewest playback interruptions. As of March 19, 2026, over 90% of YouTube’s catalog (weighted by watch time) is available in AV1. And we’re excited to begin streaming in AV2, which brings even better video quality to users and unlocks new multi-video capabilities. YouTube AV2 streams will be available for Web as soon as early 2027,” Des Keane, Engineering Director at YouTube was quoted as saying.The performance leap delivered by AV2 extends past standard video playback. Engineering leadership at Google Chrome notes that the compression gains will enable complex layout features inside internet browsers.Jim Bankoski, engineering vice president of Chrome, highlighted the broader potential of the standard:“We’re encouraged by the momentum around AV2, with partners like YouTube, Netflix, and Prime Video exploring the format and showing strong support for the technology. Beyond faster, higher-quality streaming, AV2 lays the groundwork for new browser experiences, from better multi-view video to higher-resolution, more efficient video conferencing.”The multi-video capability could allow sports fans or event viewers to watch several high-definition camera feeds simultaneously on a single monitor without exhausting system resources or network capacity.However, despite YouTube’s timeline, widespread adoption of AV2 across everyday consumer electronics will take time.Historical rollouts show that video codec adoption moves slowly through global supply chains. For comparison, the original AV1 standard was finalised back in 2018, yet commercial smartphones featuring dedicated AV1 hardware encoding did not arrive on the market until the launch of the Google Pixel 10.
Article Summary: Next-generation video compression technology promises sharper visual quality. Engineering projections indicate that AV2 is roughly 25% to 32% more efficient than its predecessor, AV1. YouTube has confirmed plans to begin rolling out AV2 streaming as early as early 2027, targeting the web browser version of the platform first.

Article Title: New York City's Knicks emailed employees free NBA championship rings, it was not what it seemed; MSG says: Using the rings as a lure to gain employees' attention was...
Article Text:
The Knicks championship ring email was built to look official

MSG says a real phishing attack led to the test

Prize-themed phishing tests draw clicks, but security agencies warn against punishing staff

Madison Square Garden Sports, the parent company of the New York Knicks, has admitted that an email offering staff free NBA championship rings was a phishing test. Employees who clicked to reserve a ring were sent to a mandatory cybersecurity class instead.The company has now called it an "unfortunate mistake." It says it will hand out more than 275 championship rings and pieces of jewellery, worth over $3.7 million, to players, coaches, employees and others in the organisation. The timing made the episode sting. The Knicks won the 2026 NBA title in June, their first since 1973, and the franchise is still in the middle of celebrating it.The email went out to a long list of MSG employees in late September, weeks before the team's ring-and-banner ceremony. According to The Athletic, which obtained a copy, it opened with a graphic of two ring styles and the line "Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here."Each employee was addressed by name and told the ring was complimentary, personalised and made by the same jeweller as the players' rings. There were two designs to pick from: Championship Gold and Garden Classic.It was an easy offer to believe. Most NBA team employees receive a ring after a title, even if it is a simpler version of what the players wear.Team sources told The Athletic that those who clicked were put through a cybersecurity class tied to owner James Dolan's growing concerns about hacking.MSG's first response to The Athletic was short: "We are not disclosing anything about the rings." A day later, the company changed course. A spokesperson said the email was a phishing simulation sent to the corporate team to strengthen its security against hackers."MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack," the statement said. It added that using the rings as a lure "was an unfortunate mistake."Phishing drills are routine at large companies, so the criticism is mostly about the bait. Guidance from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology says such exercises should not be punitive. GoDaddy faced a similar backlash in 2020, when a fake holiday bonus email to staff turned out to be a security test.From a pure security standpoint, the ring was an effective lure. Attackers often dress up phishing emails as rewards because people act on them quickly and without much thought. In a recent report, Kaspersky found that a FIFA-themed phishing simulation offering prizes for wearing a national team jersey got a 66% click rate.The trouble lies in what happens after the click. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre says punishing employees for falling for a test email can start to look like entrapment. It also advises companies to check with HR before sending anything that could upset staff, which a fake championship ring offer was always likely to do.Security tech has been a sore point at MSG for a while. The Garden has used facial recognition at its entrances since at least 2018, and in 2023 it was reported to have used the system to turn away lawyers from firms involved in litigation against the company. A database leaked earlier this year also showed MSG assigning risk scores to celebrities and their guests.MSG has not said how many employees clicked the September email, or whether it plans to change how it runs these tests.
Article Summary: The email went out to a long list of MSG employees in late September, weeks before the team's ring-and-banner ceremony. It opened with a graphic of two ring styles and the line "Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here" The company has now called it an "unfortunate mistake" and says it will hand out more than 275 rings and pieces of jewellery.

Article Title: In 2025, a developer proposed a $3.6 billion data center across 133 acres in Ohio and filed plans before a local ban; on October 20, the state Supreme Court ruled the village could keep the project on
Article Text:
Developer raced to file plans before restrictions

The timeline

Court sides with village

Massive AI-era data centre proposal

Local opposition and wider trend

A proposed $3.6 billion data centre campus in Ohio will remain on hold after the Supreme Court of Ohio ruled that local officials in the village of Lordstown do not have to continue reviewing the project while a moratorium on new data centres remains in effect. The decision stems from a dispute involving Bristolville 25 Developer LLC, which is seeking to build four three-storey data centre buildings and related infrastructure on industrial land in Lordstown, about 45 miles southeast of Cleveland. According to court records and industry reports, the development has been valued at approximately $3.6 billion and would span 133 acres across the Trumbull-Mahoning county lineThe developer began Lordstown's site-plan review process in October 2025, submitting initial plans just days before village officials moved to restrict new data centre developments. The following day, the village's planning and zoning administrator informed the company that a ban on data centres was being considered by the village council.In November 2025, Lordstown approved a ban on new data centres. The village later repealed the outright ban and replaced it with a six-month moratorium in January 2026 before extending the moratorium through the remainder of 2026.Bristolville argued that because its plans were submitted when data centres were still permitted under local zoning rules, the project should continue to be reviewed under the earlier regulations.The company sought a writ of mandamus compelling the village to move forward with the approval process.Bristolville bought the land in February 2025 and delivered its draft site plan on October 20, 2025. The next day, the village’s planning and zoning administrator told the company that a data center ban was pending before council and that review could not begin until council decided. About 100 residents, mostly opposed to new data centers, attended a council meeting in November 2025, and council voted 6-0 to ban new data centers.In January 2026, the village replaced the ban with a six-month moratorium, and council later extended it through the rest of 2026. The village engineer did an initial review after the ban passed and found missing information, including stormwater management and utility plans. Once the ban became a moratorium, the village suspended further review, and the company asked the Supreme Court to compel it to continue.In a unanimous decision issued on October 20, the state's highest court rejected the developer's claim. The court found that Bristolville had only initiated the first stage of Lordstown's four-step review process and had not completed the requirements necessary to obtain the right to apply for a zoning permit.The court concluded that because the developer had not advanced far enough through the approval process before the moratorium took effect, village officials were under no legal obligation to continue reviewing the project.Planning documents described the proposed facility as a 1.65 million-square-foot campus featuring four three-storey data centre buildings. During public discussions, project representatives said the facility would use closed-loop cooling systems and could employ around 120 people across three shifts once completed.The developer's engineering team also indicated that cooling water would initially be trucked to the site, while discussions had been held with utility provider FirstEnergy regarding the project's electricity requirements"Under the moratorium, the village is under no legal duty to proceed with a site-plan review," the court stated in its opinion.The proposal attracted significant local attention. According to reports, around 100 residents attended a village council meeting in November 2025, with most expressing opposition to additional data centre development. Village leaders said the moratorium was intended to give officials time to study potential regulations and assess the impact of such projects on the community.The ruling also adds to a series of setbacks for projects linked to Western Hospitality Partners, the New York-based company affiliated with Bristolville 25 Developer. Several proposed data centre campuses in other US states have reportedly faced opposition, zoning hurdles or infrastructure-related challenges.For now, the Ohio Supreme Court's ruling means the Lordstown project will remain frozen while the village's moratorium remains in place

Article Title: ‘The tensile fibers act like tethers’, says Nike’s Bret Schoolmeester on the science inside Apex’s Air Zoom units
Article Text:
Nike’s Apex marathon racer stacks four Air Zoom units under the forefoot

What a new weld means for the Air Zoom unit

Apex spends its whole 40mm allowance on the forefoot

Nike has spent decades learning what Air can do, and its new racers lean on it harder than ever. Apex, the marathon racer due in January 2027, packs four Air Zoom units into two stacked pairs under the forefoot, the most Air Nike has placed there, and Alphafly 4 runs a pair of the same new unit. It is a confident bet, given that Air Zoom took much of the blame when the Pegasus Premium and Vomero Premium turned out heavier than runners expected.Bret Schoolmeester, Nike’s Vice President of Running Footwear, explains the bet in four words. “Air is highly tunable,” he says. Nike can engineer a unit’s size, shape, pressure and placement around the ride it wants, and weight turned out to be one more thing it could tune.An Air Zoom unit is a sealed polymer bag of pressurised gas that compresses as the forefoot loads it and pushes back as the runner pushes off. Tensile fibres run between its top and bottom surfaces like tethers, letting Nike pressurise it hard while keeping it flat. Schoolmeester calls it “one of the highest-energy-return cushioning technologies we have tested”. Foam slowly packs out, while a sealed unit is designed to hold its behaviour for as long as it is worn.The weight fix came from the way the shell is sealed. Nike used to form the unit with heat and has moved to radio-frequency welding, which uses a high-frequency electromagnetic field to heat certain polymers from within, right at the joint. A much thinner film can be sealed that way without losing the tensile-fibre structure, and each unit came out 30 percent lighter.Getting there took what Schoolmeester has described as urgency and sleepless nights. “Confidence grew as the process repeatedly delivered consistent results, first in development and then through athlete testing,” he says, though he did not go into how every sealed unit is checked on the line.A lighter unit solved only half the problem. Apex also needed room. World Athletics caps the sole of a road racer at 40mm, insole included, and an 8mm drop maxed out at the heel leaves just 32mm under the forefoot. Apex is zero-drop at 40mm in both places, handing the whole allowance to the forefoot, where the stacked Air sits. “Zero-drop is more about the maximum propulsion in the forefoot,” Schoolmeester says.Everything else is tuned around that stack. Simulations showed two units on top of each other gave the best balance of energy return and stability. ZoomX LT foam sits beneath them, and above them a comparatively flat carbon-fibre Flyplate pushes load down so the units compress properly. The rocker and the stability come from the geometry of the whole platform, helped by a wider outsole. “Stability doesn’t necessarily come from adding more material, it comes from how you use the material you have,” he says.Nike’s numbers are up to 40 percent more energy return than Alphafly 3 at more than 10 percent less weight. The zero-drop is worth watching, since a lower drop generally asks more of the calves and Achilles, though wear testers logged more than 160km in Apex. Durability has not moved either, with Nike’s expectation for Alphafly 4 level with Alphafly 3.Nike will not say how much of that 40 percent belongs to Air, because it measures the whole system, and Swooshfly shows why. The more accessible racer has no Air Zoom at all and relies on SkyX, a foam of TPU beads steamed to different densities around the heel, plate and forefoot, which Nike compares to tuned Air. “Air Zoom and foam each offer different ways to tune a ride,” Schoolmeester says.Not long ago, Air’s weight was its limit, and a change in the factory moved it. Schoolmeester does not think Nike has reached the next one. “We do not think we have found the limits of Air yet,” he says.
Article Summary: Nike’s Apex marathon racer stacks four Air Zoom units under the forefoot. It is the most Air Nike has placed there, and Alphafly 4 runs a pair of the same new unit. Air Zoom took much of the blame when the Pegasus Premium and Vomero Premium turned out heavier than runners expected. The weight fix came from the way the shell is sealed.

Article Title: Xbox's first COO Helen Chiang leaves Microsoft after 21 years, just months after promotion; CEO Asha Sharma in memo to employees: I am ...
Article Text:
“Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,”

“We’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalised,”

“We don’t discuss individual personnel matters,”

“We’re grateful for Helen’s years of service and wish her well.”

Why Xbox created its first COO position

“end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services.”

Microsoft has lost Xbox’s first chief operating officer. Helen Chiang left the company after 21 years, about three months after she was promoted to the newly created position in July. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the departure in an internal memo, but Microsoft did not explain why Chiang was leaving.Sharma told employees in a memo reviewed by The Verge. She did not name a replacement but indicated that Xbox would retain COO leadership.she added.Microsoft also declined to explain the circumstances surrounding her exit.Xbox communications vice president Kari Perez told The Verge.As COO, Chiang was responsible for bringing Xbox’s content, hardware, platform and services businesses under one operating structure. Other Xbox leaders will divide her duties until the company finalises its plans for the position.Chiang was promoted as part of a wider reorganisation that Xbox described as a business reset. At the time, Sharma said the new position would carryP&L refers to profit-and-loss responsibility, meaning Chiang was expected to oversee how those parts of Xbox earned money, controlled costs and made investment decisions.Sharma said Chiang would “bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.”Her departure does not appear to end the COO position. For now, other Xbox leaders will handle her immediate responsibilities while the company finalises its plans.Chiang joined Microsoft in 2005 as a product manager for its Streets & Trips mapping software and moved to Xbox in 2007. She joined the Minecraft team in 2014, later became its studio head, and served as corporate vice president of the franchise. GamesRadar reported that her Xbox career included work on Xbox Live and leadership of Mojang and Minecraft.
Article Summary: Helen Chiang was promoted to the newly created position in July. She was responsible for bringing Xbox’s content, hardware, platform and services businesses under one operating structure. Other Xbox leaders will divide her duties until the company finalises its plans for the position.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says US regulation pushed China’s domestic capabilities but America's technology is ....
Article Text:
Jensen Huang.

US export curbs on China

‘American technology well prepared’

‘Companies can always use more RAM’

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said that export curbs and trade restrictions imposed by Washington have served as a ‘catalyst’ for China’s rapid progress in semiconductor development. Speaking to CNBC on the sidelines of Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, Huang stated that American regulatory measures effectively pushed China to speed up its own domestic chip manufacturing and strive for technological self-reliance. The top executive also dismissed concerns over a memory chip glut, saying that a supply surplus is unlikely to materialise by 2029.Current US trade rules prohibit the export of advanced processors to China, including Nvidia's high-end artificial intelligence (AI) GPUs. Despite these barriers, reports have claimed, several Chinese entities have managed to access that computing power through third-party data centers based in Southeast Asia. Industry experts consider this access crucial to the growing capabilities of Chinese-developed AI models.“We’ve definitely accelerated China’s initiatives, its nationalization of semiconductor manufacturing capabilities, and all of the industrial support that has been put into that sector, and so there’s no question we’ve accelerated that,” Huang said.Even with intensified competition and China’s accelerated domestic initiatives, the Nvidia chief expressed strong confidence in the standing of US technology companies. Huang stated that American tech firms remain “mighty” and are well-prepared to take on competitive pressure “from anybody.”Rejecting concerns that memory chips will be supply surplus, Huang implied that the ongoing hardware supercycle is not nearing any abrupt end."One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it," Huang said,underscoring that High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), which is a specialised form of RAM critical for Al acceleration, will continue to see widespread use for years to come.“We're the first company in the world to put LPDDR memory - what goes into your cell phones - into the world's data centers, and it's enabled us to deliver performance that's twice as energy efficient as anything in the world today, and so we're going to continue to use abundant amounts of them as well,” he said.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang says export curbs and trade restrictions imposed by Washington have served as a ‘catalyst’ for China’s rapid progress in semiconductor development. Huang also dismissed concerns over a memory chip glut, saying that a supply surplus is unlikely to materialise by 2029.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan said that they shifting their donations, just weeks after Meta CEO gifted state of California ...
Article Text:
$50 million gift backs AI and STEM expansion

The billionaire tax backdrop

Philanthropic strategy undergoes major shift

AI at the centre of both Meta and CZI

Layoffs accompany new focus

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan are doubling down on artificial intelligence, science and STEM education through both their philanthropic and corporate investments, according to a Fortune report. The couple ledged $50 million to Sacramento State University to pay for state-of-the-art STEM labs and an AI center, Fortune reports. California Governor Gavin Newsom announced the gift on January 28 and tied it to a major redevelopment of three vacant state office buildings on Sacramento’s Capitol Mall into a downtown campus. The money from Zuckerberg and Meta will cover abatement, demolition and initial construction, and will make room for new student housing alongside academic space, including STEM facilities and the AI center. Zuckerberg said the investments will strengthen communities and support the next generation of leaders and innovators. Newsom said the gift will help the school build its pipeline of talent for tech jobs, and that students need to be able to afford to live where they study.California Governor Gavin Newsom announced the donation on January 28 as part of a broader plan to transform three vacant state office buildings on Sacramento's Capitol Mall into a downtown university campus.The contribution from Meta and Zuckerberg will help fund demolition, site preparation and the initial construction phase of the project.The new campus is expected to include advanced STEM laboratories, an AI centre and student housing, with state officials framing the project as an investment in California's future workforce. Newsom said the donation would help Sacramento State strengthen its pipeline of talent for technology jobs and support students by expanding affordable housing options near campus. In a statement cited by the report, Zuckerberg said the investments would help "strengthen our communities and support the next generation of leaders and innovators. "The gift arrives as California considers a one-time 5 percent tax on billionaires’ wealth. Fortune notes that several prominent billionaires, including Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, PayPal co-founder Peter Thiel and Craft Ventures’ David Sacks, have already moved their permanent residences out of state to avoid it. Zuckerberg has made no public statement on the tax and is instead putting more money into California. He owns a compound of 11 properties in Palo Alto’s Crescent Park neighbourhood, valued at more than $110 million, and Meta has a 57-acre headquarters campus in the area plus more than 400,000 square feet of office space in nearby Menlo Park.The Sacramento donation reflects a broader change in direction at the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI), the philanthropic organisation launched by Zuckerberg and Chan in 2015. The couple recently announced that the majority of CZI's resources would be directed toward biomedical AI research, marking a shift from earlier priorities such as education and social justice initiatives.The organisation has increasingly focused on using artificial intelligence to accelerate scientific discovery and medical research. Central to that strategy is the Biohub network, a group of biomedical research institutes that aims to advance disease prevention and treatment through cutting-edge technologies.Speaking at a Biohub event in Redwood City last year, Zuckerberg described the Biohub model as one of the most impactful efforts undertaken by the organisation and said it would become the primary focus of its philanthropic work going forward.The latest donation also highlights how Zuckerberg's philanthropic goals are increasingly aligned with Meta's broader AI ambitions. Meta has committed significant resources toward developing advanced AI systems and building infrastructure to support future AI-driven products and services. Similarly, CZI is concentrating on AI-powered biomedical research, supporting work involving large-scale models for applications such as virtual cells, immune system research and disease prediction.The planned AI centre at Sacramento State fits into that vision by helping train future researchers, engineers and technology professionals while expanding access to advanced computing and STEM education.The renewed emphasis on AI and biomedical research has also led to organisational changes. Earlier this year, CZI laid off around 70 employees, primarily at its Redwood City headquarters, as it streamlined operations around its updated mission.Despite those cuts, Zuckerberg and Chan have signalled that they see AI as a transformative force for the coming decade. In a recent blog post, the couple said they were optimistic about the opportunities ahead and believed advances in AI and science could help achieve some of humanity's long-term goals.
Article Summary: The couple ledged $50 million to Sacramento State University to pay for state- of-the-art STEM labs and an AI center. California Governor Gavin Newsom announced the gift on January 28 and tied it to a major redevelopment of three vacant state office buildings on Sacramento’s Capitol Mall. Zuckerberg said the investments will strengthen communities and support the next generation of leaders and innovators.
